references.text: God promises that Sarah will bear a son named Isaac, and that He will establish His covenant with him—the immediate promise specified in Gen 17:21.
God repeats the promise that Sarah will bear a son at a set time and confirms the timing of Isaac's birth.
The promise of Isaac's birth at the appointed time is fulfilled when Sarah gives birth, and Abraham names his son Isaac.
Paul explains that it is the children of the promise who are counted as Abraham's offspring, with Isaac serving as the example of a child of promise.
God confirms His covenant with Isaac and repeats the promises given to Abraham—a fulfillment of the promise to establish the covenant with Isaac.
Sarah received power to become a mother because she trusted in Him who had made the promise—the response of faith to the promise of Isaac's birth.
Paul quotes directly from the prophecy in Genesis to support that God's promise concerning Isaac is the foundation of faith.
Both verses are part of the same covenant dialogue and show the connection between the general promise of numerous descendants and the specific heir, Isaac.
The same prophetic event told from two perspectives, together confirming God's almighty power and precise timing for Isaac's birth.
The same covenant dialogue where the general promise of many nations (v. 4) is made concrete through the specific heir, Isaac (v. 21).
Paul interprets Abraham's faith in God's power to fulfill the promise concerning Isaac, which is the very content of the prophecy in Gen 17:21.
